Alex (Sales): Hey team — pre-POC checklist for Taylor's Private deployment. Need to confirm infra readiness so SE can plan the installer run.
Maya (SE): Quick list up front: GPU drivers + CUDA, k8s version & CRI, container runtime, kernel settings (hugepages/swap off), storage perf for model weights, outbound allowlist for control plane, and a kubeconfig/bastion for our installer.
Ravi (Infra): What exact driver/CUDA versions do you need? They have A100s.
Taylor (Customer): 4x A100 40GB, Ubuntu 20.04, driver currently 470, CUDA 11.4, k8s 1.25, containerd 1.6.9. No GPU plugin installed yet.
Maya (SE): Driver 470 is pretty old for our recommended runtime. For A100s we ask for NVIDIA driver >= 510, preferably 525+. CUDA 11.8+ recommended. Also need nvidia-container-toolkit + NVIDIA device plugin for k8s.
Maya (SE): Checklist commands we ask them to run and paste back:
```
# verify GPUs
nvidia-smi -L
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv

# verify k8s nodes
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl describe node <gpu-node>
```
Ravi (Infra): Regarding k8s: we support 1.24–1.27 officially. 1.25 is OK but ensure kubelet flags include --eviction-hard and no swap. Also containerd config should have "systemd_cgroup = true".
Taylor (Customer): Noted. We can upgrade driver to 525 and CUDA to 11.8. Storage: we have 2 TB NVMe on each node + NFS for shared volumes.
Maya (SE): NVMe per node is ideal for model weights. For shared checkpoints NFS or Ceph is OK but recommend local PVCs for inference pods. Also ensure the following node labels/capabilities:
- label: redwood/gpu=true
- capacity: nvidia.com/gpu: 1 (or appropriate)

Maya (SE): Kernel tuning: disable swap, set vm.max_map_count=262144, ensure hugepages if you plan large batch sizes. Also set ulimits for filehandles: fs.file-max >= 200000.
Sasha (Security): For Private we need:
- outbound HTTPS (443) to control-plane.redwood.ai (or whatever our host will provide) for telemetry and licensing (if using hosted control plane). If fully air-gapped, we need offline install bundle.
- SSH (22) from our installer IPs (we'll provide short-lived certs) or a jumpbox
- KMS details (Vault/HSM) for key wrapping. If using HSM, provide PKCS#11 endpoint + admin contact.
- kubeconfig with a user that can create CRDs & Roles (temporary elevated creds are fine during install)
Maya (SE): Ports to open (minimum outbound): 443 (control plane), 2379/2380 not required unless we need etcd access. App traffic stays internal. For metrics/tracing we need outbound to our collector endpoints if enabled.
Taylor (Customer): We can expose a bastion with static IP. We have HashiCorp Vault in our infra. OK to provide a Vault policy for redwood-installer.
Alex (Sales): Any blockers around licensing or pricing while they upgrade drivers or storage?
Maya (SE): No pricing blocker. Timing is main thing — driver upgrade may need rebooting nodes and re-scheduling workloads. Recommend staging windows and at least one spare GPU node for testing.
Ravi (Infra): Also check OS kernel >= 5.4 for some of the newer nvidia modules. If using MIG profiles on A100, ensure driver supports MIG and configure profiles ahead of time.
Maya (SE): For the installer we need these artifacts before run (send securely):
- kubeconfig (cluster-admin or equivalent) as a file
- bastion public IP + SSH user/key or short-lived cert
- Vault address + role/policy config (if using KMS)
- OIDC issuer URL (if we need to mint SA tokens)
- Storage class names for fast/slow PVCs

deploy-bot: Installer ticket created #POC-5421 — assign to @Maya (SE). Logs will be posted in this thread during install.
Taylor (Customer): I'll collect kubeconfig and bastion info and upload to the secure portal. ETA tomorrow morning.
Maya (SE): Great — when you post the output of `nvidia-smi -L` and `kubectl get nodes -o wide` we'll sign off on readiness and schedule the install. If anything else pops up we'll ping here.
Alex (Sales): Thanks all — I'll keep the customer updated on scheduling and re: maintenance window for driver upgrades. :thumbsup:
